reversals.own_notes_doc: Mon: Finished ripping Polars out of the feature pipeline. Every module now imports pandas only, and polars is gone from requirements.txt. Tue: Rewrote the lag-feature code with pandas groupby and shift. A bit slower, but the team's tooling all expects pandas DataFrames, so this is simpler for everyone. Wed: Updated the data-loading helpers to use pandas read_parquet with the pyarrow engine. Thu: Ran the full test suite, all green. Fri: Still need to delete the old lazy-query helpers that nobody calls anymore and update the README examples so they show pandas code.

reversals.own_notes_doc: Workflow changes, started this month. No more Jupyter. Every experiment is now a Python script under experiments/ with its own config file, run from the terminal. I step through problems with breakpoints in the VS Code debugger instead of rerunning cells. Plots get saved to outputs/ as PNG files. Archived the old .ipynb files in a zip and removed the Jupyter kernel from the environment. So far this has cut hidden-state bugs to zero. Next: add a Makefile target for each experiment and write a short checklist for starting new scripts.

reversals.own_notes_doc: Tooling decisions, May. Moved my main work to R. The team's statistical reporting is all in R Markdown, and the tidyverse fits how I think about data. Installed RStudio, dplyr, ggplot2, and fable for forecasting. Ported the weekly report script from Python. It is now shorter and the plots look better. Keeping one old Python environment around only for legacy jobs, but all new code is written in R. To do: learn the targets package for pipelines and set up renv so each project is reproducible.
